newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian inflation falls for fifth successive month.
newsitem.headline: Italian inflation falls for fifth successive month.

text.p: Italian inflation fell for the fifth consecutive month in June, dipping to 1.4 percent year-on-year from 1.6 percent in May, national statistics office Istat said Friday.
On a month-on-month basis, inflation remained unchanged.
Friday's data confirmed earlier preliminary figures from leading Italian cities and means the country's inflation rate is now at its lowest level since February 1969.
Istat said the inflation rate in the first six months of the year was 2.0 percent, compared with the same period in 1996, while average inflation over the last 12 months was 2.5 percent.
However, the consumer price index appears set to climb again in the second half of the year for largely technical and statistical reasons.

The official inflation goal for 1997 as a whole is 2.5 percent, but Italy's centre-left government has said the recent sharp slowdown means it will certainly come in under target, despite the forecast pick-up in price pressure.
Price growth has tailed off sharply over the past year, with inflation last June standing at 3.9 percent.
Economists say the fall has been largely due to depressed domestic demand, the high cost of credit with a stronger lira and a favourable trend in international commodity prices.

Recognising the decline in inflation, the Bank of Italy trimmed its official discount rate to 6.25 percent last Friday, a cut of 50 basis points. It was the fourth time in less than 12 months that the central bank had reduced rates.
